answer: A refundable identity bond stops Sybils by making each fake account cost real capital upfront. Like a karst cave that admits only one narrow passage, each agent locks a bond that is slashed if duplicates or fraud are found, so one person cannot cheaply run thousands of identities. An attacker must fund a separate bond for every fake, like carving a new glacier channel each time, tying up capital that cannot be reused elsewhere, and a wharf-side audit that links fraud revokes the whole cluster, so the cost rises with each fake while honest agents pay only once and get their bond back.
